guideTitle: 6 Best Portable Hose Reel Carts in 2026
metaTitle: 6 Best Portable Hose Reel Carts in 2026
metaDescription: Six portable hose reel carts compared on weight, wheel size, resin versus metal, assembly and storage footprint, for easy moving around a small or medium yard.
introParagraphs: Portable is about more than wheels. A truly portable hose reel cart is light enough to lift over a step, small enough to tuck beside a faucet, and ready to use without an hour of assembly. The biggest long-run carts are not portable in practice, because the loaded weight of 250 or 300 feet of hose makes a four-wheel cart a chore to carry up stairs or stow in a crowded garage.

This lineup focuses on easy-moving options. Two generic 175 foot resin carts both list 7 inch wheels, one arriving fully assembled with a glove compartment and the other measuring about 24 x 20 x 32 inches. The GrillTown Hosemobile holds 175 feet in assembled resin, the VEVOR 175 foot uses steel on two PVC wheels, the Yestar holds 75 to 150 feet with an adjustable handrail, and the Giraffe Tools handles 150 feet of 5/8 inch hose or 200 feet of 1/2 inch hose on a low center of gravity.

We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on weight-related design, wheels, assembly effort and storage size. Capacity ratings assume a standard hose, and where a listing leaves out a detail, we say so.

products.name: 175 ft Portable Hose Reel Cart With 7 Inch Wheels
products.description:
This generic 175 foot cart holds up to 175 feet of standard 5/8 inch hose and arrives fully assembled, so you attach your hose and start winding with no tools. Its 7 inch oversized wheels are described as giving better traction on grass, gravel or dirt. The body is weather-resistant resin that resists cracking and fading, and a small compartment holds gloves and connectors.

A handle hook secures the end of the leader hose so the hose does not unravel after winding, and a leader hose is included. The ready-to-use setup is the main portability win, since many metal carts need an hour of bolt tightening. Resin keeps the weight down for lifting over a step or curb.

The tradeoff is that resin is less robust than steel under heavy loads, and the listing does not state the cart's weight or exact dimensions. Generic branding also means less documented support than a named maker. In ownership terms, the assembled setup is a relief, and the compartment saves a trip back to the garage for a spare washer. Compared with the compact resin 175 foot cart, it matches the 7 inch wheels but trades the stated 24 x 20 x 32 inch footprint for a built-in storage compartment. Compared with the VEVOR 175 foot, which sits on two PVC wheels and needs assembly, it is easier to start with. It suits buyers who want to start winding today.
products.bestFor: Medium yards where ready-to-use assembly and larger wheels matter.
pros: 7 inch wheels for grass and gravel
Handle hook holds the hose end
Small compartment for gloves and fittings

products.name: 175 ft Compact Resin 2-Wheel Hose Reel Cart
products.description:
This resin cart holds up to 175 feet of standard 5/8 inch hose in a compact body measuring about 24 inches wide, 20 deep and 32 high. The weather-resistant resin shrugs off wind and rain, and the listing also mentions a durable metal frame under the shell. Two 7 inch wheels keep it light and easy to tilt, even when loaded with a full hose.

Resin is lighter than steel and will not rust, which helps portability and keeps upkeep low. The stated dimensions are useful for deciding whether it fits beside a garage wall or in a shed. It arrives ready to use with no assembly, and a water hose for connection is included along with a built-in safety hook that stops the hose end from slipping.

The tradeoff is that resin can crack in extreme cold or after years of strong sun, and it feels less robust than steel. A two-wheel design also means the cart does not stand on its own once you let go, so you will lean it against something while you connect the hose. Its footprint is small enough that it works on a patio without dominating the space. Compared with the 7 inch wheel cart above, it publishes dimensions but has no listed glove compartment. Compared with the GrillTown Hosemobile, which stands 45 inches tall, it is a lower 32 inches and easier to tuck under a shelf. It suits small yards and tight storage.
products.bestFor: Small yards and tight storage where weight and footprint matter.
cons: Two-wheel design will not stand alone

products.name: GrillTown Hosemobile 175 ft Hose Reel Cart

specList.label: Dimensions
specList.value: 22 w x 45 h x 22.8 l inches

products.description:
The Hosemobile holds 175 feet of 5/8 inch hose, arrives fully assembled and uses sturdy resin construction. Its Easylink system is meant to give a watertight connection between the reel and your hoses. The listed dimensions are 22 inches wide, 45 inches high and 22.8 inches long, which makes it taller than the other resin carts here.

Fully assembled means no tools and no lost screws. Resin keeps the weight down compared with a steel frame, which helps when you wheel it around a yard. The extra height gives the drum room to wind evenly and keeps the crank at a comfortable level for many adults.

The tradeoff is that the listing gives no wheel size, no crank detail and no finish information, so check the product page for those before you buy. At 45 inches tall it needs more headroom in a shed than the 32 inch compact resin cart. Resin is also less robust than steel under heavy load. In ownership terms, expect basic function with a plain no-frills design. Compared with the generic 7 inch wheel cart, it gives you a named maker and published dimensions but no storage compartment. Compared with the VEVOR 175 foot, it is lighter but less rugged. It suits buyers who want simplicity from a recognizable name.
products.bestFor: Casual users who want a ready-to-roll resin cart from a named maker.
cons: Wheel size not stated in the listing

products.name: VEVOR 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.description:
The VEVOR 175 foot cart holds up to 175 feet of 5/8 inch hose, with hose not included. The structure is sturdy powder-coated steel with a weather-resistant coating and brass fittings, and a non-slip handle is meant to ease winding. The listing describes a low center of gravity and two solid PVC wheels for various terrains.

Steel gives it a more solid feel than the resin carts. At 175 feet the size remains manageable, so it is a balanced choice between strength and weight. Brass fittings resist leaks and rust, and the non-slip handle helps with wet hands after a car wash or a rainy morning.

The tradeoff is that steel is heavier than resin and can rust if the coating chips, so touch up any scratches. The listing does not give wheel diameter, and there are only two wheels, so it will not stand alone like the four-wheel carts. Assembly is also required, unlike the two fully assembled resin carts. In ownership terms, plan for some bolt tightening on day one and a periodic check of the coating. Compared with the generic 7 inch wheel cart, it is sturdier but needs assembly. Compared with the Giraffe Tools, it holds 175 feet of 5/8 inch hose against the Giraffe's 150 feet. It suits buyers who want durability in a medium size.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a steel cart that is still manageable to move.
cons: Needs assembly, wheel size not stated

products.name: Yestar Portable Hose Reel Cart With Adjustable Handrail
specs: Holds 75 to 150 ft of 5/8 inch hose
products.description:
The Yestar cart holds 75 to 150 feet of 5/8 inch hose and has an adjustable handrail that you set to your height with a carabiner design. The reel frame is weather-resistant powder-coated metal with an aluminum tube support and plastic fittings. A non-slip handle helps keep the hose from kinking as you wind it.

An adjustable handrail is rare in this category and helps with ergonomics, especially if you are very tall or short. The metal frame with an aluminum support keeps the weight modest. The maker says setup takes about 10 minutes and points to an installation video, which is quick for a metal cart.

The tradeoff is capacity, since 75 to 150 feet is the smallest range among the full carts here. Plastic fittings can wear over time, and the listing does not state wheel size. The maker also says to contact them if screws are missing, which suggests checking the hardware bag when you unbox it. In ownership terms, setting the handrail height once is quick, and the smaller reel is easy to store. Compared with the VEVOR 175 foot, it holds up to 25 feet less at the top of its range. Compared with the Giraffe Tools at 150 feet of 5/8 inch hose, it matches the top end but has no low-center-of-gravity claim. It suits smaller yards.
products.bestFor: Smaller yards where handle height needs to suit the user.

products.name: Giraffe Tools 200 ft Hose Reel Cart 1/2 Inch
specs: 150 ft of 5/8 or 200 ft of 1/2 inch

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: 150 ft of 5/8 inch or 200 ft of 1/2 inch

products.description:
This Giraffe Tools cart holds 150 feet of 5/8 inch hose or 200 feet of 1/2 inch hose, and it does not accept 3/4 inch hose. A low center of gravity reduces tipping when you pull hose out, and two solid explosion-proof knobby tires help on most surfaces. The heavy-duty metal frame has a powder finish, and a solid brass connector aims to keep it leak-proof.

A low center of gravity helps when you tow the cart behind you, since a top-heavy reel tips on bumps. A hose guide system lays the hose on neatly while you turn the non-slip handle. Many parts are pre-assembled, and the instructions list every component, so setup is a few steps.

The tradeoff is that the 200 foot figure applies only to thinner 1/2 inch hose, and a 5/8 inch hose gets 150 feet. It is metal, so it is heavier than the resin carts, and the listing gives no tire diameter. A 5 foot lead-in hose is fitted, but it is short, so plan your spigot position. In ownership terms, stability is the reason to choose it, and the brass connector means fewer drips at the spigot. Compared with the VEVOR 175 foot, it holds 25 feet less of 5/8 inch hose but promises more steadiness. Compared with the Yestar, which tops out at 150 feet, it matches that figure for 5/8 inch hose and adds the 200 foot thin-hose option. It suits buyers who tow the cart often.
products.bestFor: Buyers who tow the cart often and worry about tipping.
pros: Low center of gravity limits tipping

buyingCriteria.explanation: Resin is lighter than steel, which helps portability, and it will not rust. A cart you cannot lift over a step or into a trunk is not portable in practice, so think about your own carrying tolerance. The two generic 175 foot resin carts and the GrillTown Hosemobile use resin, while the VEVOR 175 foot and Giraffe Tools use steel or metal. Resin can crack in hard freezes or after years of sun, so store it in shade, whereas steel needs its coating checked for chips.

Bigger wheels roll better over lawns and gravel, and small casters dig into soft ground. Both generic resin carts list 7 inch wheels, which is a reasonable minimum for grass. The VEVOR 175 foot and Giraffe Tools both use two wheels without stating a diameter, so check the product page if your yard is lumpy. A two-wheel cart tilts back and does not stand alone, which is fine for short hauls but tiring over long distances.

Portable should also mean ready to use. The generic 7 inch wheel cart and the GrillTown Hosemobile arrive fully assembled, and the compact resin cart needs no assembly either. The Yestar takes about 10 minutes and the Giraffe Tools is mostly pre-assembled, while the VEVOR needs real assembly. If you dislike hardware bags, favor the assembled carts and save an hour of work.

A portable cart still has to live somewhere between uses. The compact resin cart states about 24 x 20 x 32 inches, while the GrillTown Hosemobile is 22 wide by 45 high by 22.8 long. Measure the shelf, shed doorway or garage corner before buying, since a tall cart may not slide under a bench. Smaller reels such as the Yestar at 75 to 150 feet are easiest to tuck away.

Ratings assume a standard 5/8 inch hose, and a thicker hose lowers real length because the drum fills sooner. Most picks here rate 175 feet, the Yestar rates 75 to 150 feet, and the Giraffe Tools rates 150 feet of 5/8 inch hose or 200 feet of 1/2 inch. The Giraffe explicitly does not accept 3/4 inch hose. Buy a cart rated for more length than your hose to avoid overfilling, which causes uneven winding.

A tipping cart is not portable in practice, because you spend the afternoon righting it. The Giraffe Tools has a low center of gravity and a hose guide system, and the VEVOR also advertises a low center of gravity. The Yestar's adjustable handrail lets you set the grip height, which reduces back strain. Choose handle comfort for your own height, since a handle that is too low forces you to stoop on every haul.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and material
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared resin and metal builds as described on each listing. The two generic resin carts and the GrillTown Hosemobile lead on lightness, while the VEVOR and Giraffe Tools lead on sturdiness. Lighter carts earned more credit for portability, and heavier ones lost points unless they offered something in return, such as stability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Setup
howWeEvaluated.description: Assembly state was reviewed from the product pages. The generic 7 inch wheel cart and the GrillTown Hosemobile arrive fully assembled, and the compact resin cart needs none. The Yestar takes about 10 minutes and the Giraffe Tools is mostly pre-assembled, so a portable cart that needs real work ranked lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mobility
howWeEvaluated.description: Wheel details and stability were weighed together. Both generic resin carts list 7 inch wheels, and the Giraffe Tools lists a low center of gravity with knobby tires. Carts that left out wheel size, such as the Yestar and GrillTown, were marked down for the missing detail.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: Stated ratings drove this score. The 175 foot carts rate 5/8 inch hose, the Giraffe Tools rates 150 feet of 5/8 inch or 200 feet of 1/2 inch, and the Yestar rates 75 to 150 feet. The VEVOR leads on 5/8 inch capacity among the metal carts at 175 feet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ergonomics and value
howWeEvaluated.description: Handles, hooks and storage extras were noted. The Yestar's adjustable handrail stands out, the VEVOR has a non-slip handle, and the generic 7 inch wheel cart adds a handle hook and a storage compartment. We weighed these features against how much each cart restricts hose length.

faq.q: What makes a hose reel cart portable?
faq.a: Low weight, decent wheels, easy assembly and a small footprint are the main factors. Resin carts such as the compact 175 foot model with 7 inch wheels are lighter than steel ones. Check wheel size and dimensions on the listing, since some makers leave them out.

faq.q: Should I choose resin or steel?
faq.a: Resin is light and rust-free, which suits lifting and moving. Steel is stronger and steadier, which suits towing and rougher ground. The compact resin cart and the VEVOR 175 foot show the two ends of that tradeoff.

faq.q: How much hose will a portable cart really hold?
faq.a: The 175 foot carts rate 5/8 inch hose, and the Giraffe Tools rates 150 feet of 5/8 inch or 200 feet of 1/2 inch. A thicker hose lowers real length, and the Giraffe does not accept 3/4 inch hose at all. Leave a few feet of spare drum space, because overfilling causes uneven winding.

faq.q: Will a two-wheel cart tip over?
faq.a: It can, since it does not stand alone once you let go. The Giraffe Tools has a low center of gravity to help while towing. Avoid overfilling, and lean the cart against a wall when you connect the hose.

The generic 7 inch wheel cart and the GrillTown Hosemobile arrive fully assembled, and the compact resin cart needs no assembly. The Giraffe Tools is mostly pre-assembled, the Yestar takes about 10 minutes, and the VEVOR needs real assembly. Check the hardware bag before you start.

faq.q: How should I store a hose cart?
faq.a: Drain the hose before winding and store the cart out of direct sun when you can. Resin can degrade under strong UV and crack in a hard freeze. Measure your shed first, since the GrillTown Hosemobile is 45 inches tall while the compact resin cart is 32.

faq.q: Can I use an expandable hose on these carts?
faq.a: It is not a good idea, because expandable hoses swell when pressurized and some makers say reels are not suited to them. The listings here rate standard 5/8 inch or 1/2 inch hose. If you like a lightweight hose, check with the cart maker before buying.
